newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on Dow and retail data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on Dow and retail data.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed down on Thursday after dealers took profits on record gains chalked up earlier in the week, spurred by a slump on Wall Street and disappointing retail sales figures, traders said.

"Profit-taking held sway throughout the session, and the late fall by the Dow Jones dragged us down towards the close, which was almost inevitable after yesterday's record," a trader from the Vector brokerage said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 35.31 points, or 0.91 percent, at 3,839.73. Trading volume was moderate at 86.6 million shares traded.
The Dow Jones closed down 1.32 percent to 6,927.38 points.
Other traders said disappointing retail sales data also cooled investor sentiment.
"Evidently consumption has yet to recover. Although there have been good macroeconomic figures, the microeconomic picture is still bleak," a floor trader said.

Mexico's National Statistics Institute INEGI announced in late trade that retail sales in December fell 1.9 percent in year-ago terms, although wholesale figures were up 9.2 percent for the same period.
Dealers said that foreign investors were conspicuously absent during the session, as evidenced by mediocre volume figures.

"The day was lackluster. Both locals and foreigners were in the market, but the latter were thin on the ground. The thing is that most dealers were expecting a sharper fall, so I suppose they were sitting on the sidelines," one broker said.
Profit-taking on Telmex L shares, which accounted for one-fifth of all shares traded, weighed heavily on the market. Telmex ended off 20 centavos at 15.52 pesos, while its ADRs fell 7/8 to 39-7/8.
Retail stock Commerci UBC share units shrugged off retail data news and gained 22 centavos to 7.54 pesos, while its UB units were up 18 centavos to 7.46 pesos.
Traders said the market bought the stock heavily on speculation Commerci would announce a joint venture with a major U.S. partner.

In percentage terms, the most notable gainer was mining company Autlan up 19 centavos to 3.97 pesos. Dealers said they bought on speculation the firm was to buy Venezuelan firm Ferrosilicios, which supplies raw material to make steel alloys.
Financial group Bancomer was a notable decliner off 13 centavos at 3.13 pesos on what traders said was profit-taking coupled with concerns over the weakness of the banking system.
